readings.name: The forgiven servant must become merciful
readings.outcome: A distinct movement from received remission to present obligation. Chrysostom’s disproportionate gift and repeated plea, Augustine’s daily debtor/creditor dependence and correction, and Aquinas’s later distinction are explained as arguments. All seventeen conditional/base elements contribute, with a separate literal, allegorical, moral and anagogical distillation.

readings.name: God guards his people on an unfinished journey
readings.outcome: A distinct movement from deliverance through trial to final rest. Gregory’s permission and without-cause distinctions, Augustine’s whole-Christ Caph and martyr-help argument, and Chrysostom’s Passover journey are developed. All seventeen elements contribute, with each of the four senses retained.

semantic_review.comparison: Page 22 demonstrates different functions for Job and the Gospel within the two readings. It preserves future judgment versus Schuster’s present privation of truth, and expressly identifies the whole-formulary constructions as editorial synthesis.
semantic_review.source_roles: Historical study English, biblical comparators, adapted chants, acquired transcriptions, later doctrinal explanation and modern introductions remain distinguished. No new model translation or historical compositional-intent claim was identified.

consequential_loci.source: Chrysostom, Homilies on Matthew, NPNF I.10, retained CCEL historical English
consequential_loci.inspection: Retained source text read at the specified loci and surrounding argument.
consequential_loci.outcome: The prior divine gifts, remission exceeding the plea, repeated plea and refused patience, real pardon and its revocation, unending until, and forgiveness from the heart support the study’s mercy argument. The prose explains the actual asymmetry and inference.

consequential_loci.source: Augustine, Sermon 83 (NPNF I.6, Sermon XXXIII), retained CCEL historical English
consequential_loci.inspection: Retained source text read at the specified loci and surrounding argument.
consequential_loci.outcome: The simultaneous debtor/creditor, beggar and living bread, daily petition, re-exacted forgiven debt, and inward pardon with correction are present. The study distinguishes Augustine’s correction principle from its later protective applications and from ancient disciplinary practices.

consequential_loci.source: Aquinas, Summa theologiae III, question 88, English Dominican translation
consequential_loci.inspection: Retained source text read at the specified loci and surrounding argument.
consequential_loci.outcome: The study correctly explains new mortal fault, ingratitude for earlier pardon, virtual return of debt rather than undone divine pardon, and the non-arithmetic measure of renewed liability. Its later technical account is not attributed to Chrysostom or Augustine.

consequential_loci.source: Gregory the Great, Moralia in Job, Library of Fathers historical English in the retained Lectionary Central transcription
consequential_loci.inspection: Retained source text read at the specified loci and surrounding argument.
consequential_loci.outcome: The source distinguishes evil will from permitted power, absence of antecedent punitive guilt from manifestation and growth of virtue, anthropopathic moved language, and Job’s simultaneous presence in the afflicter’s and helper’s hands. The study teaches these distinctions and does not license diagnosing a neighbor’s suffering.

consequential_loci.source: Augustine, Expositions of the Psalms, retained NPNF I.8 historical English
consequential_loci.loci: Vulgate Psalm 89 sections 1–4 (NPNF 90); Psalm 113 sections 1–6 (NPNF 114); Psalm 118 Aleph verses 1–8 and Caph verses 81–88 (NPNF 119)
consequential_loci.inspection: Retained source text read at the specified loci and surrounding argument.
consequential_loci.outcome: Refuge and divine immutability, caution about Mosaic authorship, baptismal Exodus and subsequent falls, grace-enabled conduct, longing toward salvation, the whole Christ and martyrs, and help preserved through death support the cited claims. The omitted chant words remain distinguished from the full biblical context.

consequential_loci.loci: XXII on Ephesians 6:9–13 and editorial notes 465, 468; XXIII complete; XXIV exposition of 6:14–22 and following faith/prayer argument
consequential_loci.inspection: Retained source text read at the specified loci and surrounding argument.
